correctness.rationale: For disjoint vertex sets of sizes h and k, two specified connected-component events share exactly hk required absent cross-edges, so P(A_S and B_T)=P(A_S)P(B_T)(1-p)^(-hk). Intersecting vertex sets cannot both be distinct components. Summing over disjoint sets gives E(C_H*C_K)=mu_H*mu_K[(n-h)_k/(n)_k](1-p)^(-hk), hence exact covariance and rank-one cross-size block, with a unique positive sign-switch p*. The negative log of 1-p* is the rectangular average of log((n-a-b)/(n-a-b-1)); strictly increasing summands establish threshold ordering whenever both size pairs feasible. Taylor expansion yields p*=1/n+(h+k-2)/(2*n*n)+O(n^-3). At p=1/n+lambda/n^2, tree-leading means E[X_j]=n*tau_j(1)+O(1) and bracket=hk(lambda-(h+k-2)/2)/n^2+O(n^-3), giving the finite critical-window covariance. Domain h!=k, h+k<=n, 0<p<1, fixed h,k for asymptotics. Independent exact-Fraction enumeration of labeled G(n,p), n=4,5,6 and 3 rational p values checked mixed factorial moments; enumeration is not the universal proof.
residual_risks: The rank-one statement excludes same-size covariance blocks, whose diagonals include identical-component terms.
The p=1/n+lambda/n^2 expansion is fixed-size, not uniform for h,k growing with n; at finite n choose p in (0,1).
